title: Build an O(1) LRU cache
summary: Implement a fixed-capacity least-recently-used cache whose get and put are both O(1), then prove it holds up under a large workload.
brief_md:
We keep recomputing expensive results and our memory keeps growing. Build us a **fixed-capacity LRU cache**: a bounded key/value store that, when full, evicts the *least-recently-used* entry to make room.

The whole point of this module is that the complexity of the data structure you choose is part of the contract, so the headline requirement is performance: **`get` and `put` must both be O(1) amortised**, not O(n). A version that scans a list to find the least-recently-used key on every write will pass the small correctness tests and then fall over in production — the final milestone exists to catch exactly that.

Build a `LRUCache` class in `lru.py` with this contract:

- `LRUCache(capacity)` — `capacity` is a positive integer; a non-positive capacity raises `ValueError`.
- `put(key, value)` — insert or update. Updating an existing key refreshes its recency. When the cache is at capacity and a *new* key arrives, evict the least-recently-used key first.
- `get(key)` — return the value and mark the key most-recently-used. A missing key raises `KeyError` (and counts as a miss).
- `key in cache` — a non-mutating peek: it must **not** change recency or the hit/miss counters.
- `len(cache)` — current number of stored entries.
- `cache.stats` — a dict `{"hits": int, "misses": int}` counting `get` outcomes.
- `repr(cache)` — includes the capacity and current size.

Use the container that makes the recency operations O(1). `collections.OrderedDict` (with `move_to_end` and `popitem(last=False)`) is the intended tool; a hand-rolled dict-plus-doubly-linked-list is also accepted. Do not reach for `functools.lru_cache` — the exercise is to build the mechanism, not call it.
requirements: `get` and `put` are both O(1) amortised — no linear scan per operation.
`put` on a full cache evicts the least-recently-used key before inserting a new one.
Both `get` and `put` on an existing key refresh that key's recency.
`get` on a missing key raises `KeyError`; a non-positive capacity raises `ValueError`.
`in` is a non-mutating peek; `len`, `stats` and `repr` behave as specified.
Recency and eviction are backed by an O(1) structure (OrderedDict or a linked list), not a re-sorted list.
constraints: Do not use `functools.lru_cache` or any third-party cache library — build the mechanism yourself.
No linear scan (`min`, `.index`, re-sorting the keys) on the hot path of `get`/`put`.
non_goals: Time-based expiry (TTL) — eviction is purely by recency and capacity.

milestones.title: Core store: put, get, and the two error contracts
milestones.description_md: Get the basic store working. `put` inserts, `get` returns the value or raises `KeyError`, `len` reflects the count, and constructing with a non-positive capacity raises `ValueError`. Recency and eviction come next — for now just store and retrieve.

tests.name: put then get returns the stored value
tests.body:
import pytest

from lru import LRUCache


def test_put_then_get():
    c = LRUCache(2)
    c.put("a", 1)
    assert c.get("a") == 1


def test_update_existing_key_changes_value_not_size():
    c = LRUCache(2)
    c.put("a", 1)
    c.put("a", 99)
    assert c.get("a") == 99
    assert len(c) == 1


def test_missing_key_raises_keyerror():
    c = LRUCache(2)
    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        c.get("nope")


def test_non_positive_capacity_raises_valueerror():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        LRUCache(0)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        LRUCache(-3)


def test_len_tracks_entries():
    c = LRUCache(3)
    assert len(c) == 0
    c.put("a", 1)
    c.put("b", 2)
    assert len(c) == 2

milestones.title: Recency and eviction
milestones.description_md: Make it a real LRU. When the cache is full and a new key arrives, evict the least-recently-used entry. Both `get` and `put` on an existing key must move that key to most-recently-used, so a key you keep touching is never the one evicted. This is the milestone where the choice of an O(1) recency structure starts to matter.

tests.name: a full cache evicts the least-recently-used key
tests.body:
import pytest

from lru import LRUCache


def test_evicts_least_recently_used():
    c = LRUCache(2)
    c.put("a", 1)
    c.put("b", 2)
    c.put("c", 3)          # 'a' is LRU -> evicted
    assert "a" not in c
    assert c.get("b") == 2
    assert c.get("c") == 3


def test_get_refreshes_recency():
    c = LRUCache(2)
    c.put("a", 1)
    c.put("b", 2)
    assert c.get("a") == 1   # 'a' now most-recently-used, 'b' is LRU
    c.put("c", 3)            # evicts 'b', not 'a'
    assert "b" not in c
    assert c.get("a") == 1


def test_put_on_existing_key_refreshes_recency():
    c = LRUCache(2)
    c.put("a", 1)
    c.put("b", 2)
    c.put("a", 10)           # updating 'a' makes it MRU, 'b' is LRU
    c.put("c", 3)            # evicts 'b'
    assert "b" not in c
    assert c.get("a") == 10

milestones.title: Introspection: in, stats and repr
milestones.description_md: Round out the type's protocols. `key in cache` is a non-mutating peek — it must not change recency and must not touch the hit/miss counters. `cache.stats` reports `{"hits", "misses"}` accumulated by `get`. `repr(cache)` shows the capacity and current size so it is useful in a debugger.

tests.name: `in` peeks without changing recency or counters
tests.body:
from lru import LRUCache


def test_contains_does_not_change_recency():
    c = LRUCache(2)
    c.put("a", 1)
    c.put("b", 2)
    assert ("a" in c) is True     # peek must NOT refresh 'a'
    c.put("c", 3)                 # 'a' is still LRU -> evicted
    assert "a" not in c


def test_contains_does_not_count_as_hit_or_miss():
    c = LRUCache(2)
    c.put("a", 1)
    _ = "a" in c
    _ = "z" in c
    assert c.stats == {"hits": 0, "misses": 0}

tests.name: stats counts get outcomes; repr shows capacity and size
tests.body:
import pytest

from lru import LRUCache


def test_stats_counts_hits_and_misses():
    c = LRUCache(2)
    c.put("a", 1)
    c.get("a")
    c.get("a")
    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        c.get("missing")
    assert c.stats == {"hits": 2, "misses": 1}


def test_repr_shows_capacity_and_size():
    c = LRUCache(5)
    c.put("a", 1)
    text = repr(c)
    assert "5" in text and "1" in text

milestones.title: Prove it is O(1) under load
milestones.description_md: The correctness tests above pass for an O(n) implementation too. This milestone runs a large workload — hundreds of thousands of operations against a bounded cache — and asserts the results are correct. A per-operation linear scan turns this into hundreds of millions of steps and blows the sandbox timeout; an O(1) OrderedDict-based implementation finishes comfortably. Passing here is your evidence that the complexity contract actually holds.

tests.name: a large workload stays correct (and fast enough not to time out)
tests.body:
from lru import LRUCache


def test_large_workload_is_correct_and_bounded():
    capacity = 2000
    c = LRUCache(capacity)
    n = 400_000
    # Insert 0..n; only the most recent `capacity` keys should survive.
    for i in range(n):
        c.put(i, i * 2)
    assert len(c) == capacity
    # The oldest keys were evicted long ago...
    assert 0 not in c
    assert (n - capacity - 1) not in c
    # ...and the most recent `capacity` keys are all present with correct values.
    for i in range(n - capacity, n):
        assert c.get(i) == i * 2


def test_hot_key_is_never_evicted():
    c = LRUCache(100)
    c.put("hot", "v")
    for i in range(50_000):
        c.put(i, i)          # constant churn of cold keys
        assert c.get("hot") == "v"   # touching 'hot' keeps it MRU forever
    assert "hot" in c

rubric.description: Core store works: put/get round-trip, KeyError on miss, ValueError on bad capacity, len is accurate.
Correct LRU semantics: eviction removes the true least-recently-used key, and both get and put refresh recency.
Protocols are correct: `in` is a non-mutating peek, stats counts get outcomes, repr is informative.
Operations are O(1) amortised — the large-workload milestone passes within the sandbox timeout.

stretch_goals: Add a `capacity` setter that shrinks the cache, evicting LRU entries until it fits.
Add `peek(key)` that returns the value without refreshing recency or touching stats.
Add a `hit_rate` property derived from stats, defined to be 0.0 before any get.
